analysis.title: ECB Preview: On Hold Amid Twin Shocks
key_insights: Berenberg expects the ECB to leave policy rates unchanged on Thursday 29 October and repeat a data-dependent, meeting-by-meeting approach. The ECB raised rates by 25bps in both June and September in response to higher energy prices.
Berenberg expects the next hike most likely on 17 December, when new staff projections are presented, after the pause on 29 October. Both 2026 hikes came at meetings with new projections.
Eurozone headline inflation rose to a three-year high of 3.8% yoy in September. At current oil prices it may briefly breach 4% in coming months and stay above 3% at least until spring 2027.

The ECB may signal that 2027 average inflation at current energy prices could be closer to its adverse scenario of 3.2% than the 2.5% baseline from 10 September. The report expects the ECB to say the risks to inflation have tilted further to the upside.

Since 8 September, 10-year yields are up 78bp for France and 38bp for Italy, while the German Bund yield is near its level of six weeks ago. Berenberg says higher risk premia in long yields reduce the perceived need for the ECB to hike at the short end.
Berenberg does not expect a change in the pace of balance sheet reduction. Maturing bonds from previous asset purchase programmes will keep rolling off without reinvestment.

Berenberg does not expect direct ECB support for France. The ECB could use liquidity injections into short-term funding markets or the Transmission Protection Instrument (TPI) to shield Italy and others from contagion in a dramatically worse crisis. It would support France only if Paris returns to more sustainable policies. A cautiously worded verbal intervention is possible only if the French spread blows out disorderly and by far more than fundamentals warrant.
The Strait of Hormuz situation may or may not change after the US midterm elections on 3 November, possibly through renewed US attacks on Iran followed by negotiations. The ECB may wait for clarity.
The Eurozone Composite Output flash PMI fell to a four-month low of 51.9 in October from 53.1 in September, which could precede a loss of growth momentum.

Berenberg argues the case for further hikes is weaker than it looks. Eight months after the Iran war began it sees little evidence of second-round effects such as a price-wage spiral. The October PMI showed output price inflation slowed despite a surge in input price inflation.
If oil prices fall through next year as Berenberg expects, and the effect is visible by the March 2027 meeting, the ECB will likely end the hike-pause pattern then and stay on hold through 2027.

Lagarde looks set to leave office early next year, probably in January, so a successor can be appointed while Macron is still in office before the April/May 2027 French presidential election. It would be a surprise if she announced a firm departure date on Thursday.

EU leaders will likely fill three ECB Executive Board vacancies opening in 2027 as a package by the EU summit of 17-18 December. Klaas Knot and Pablo Hernandez de Cos remain favourites to succeed Lagarde, and Knot may have an edge from his past chairing of the Financial Stability Board.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Three-year high. It supports the case for another ECB hike, most likely in December.
At current oil prices inflation may briefly breach 4%. It looks set to stay above 3% until at least spring 2027.
The ECB may signal that at current energy prices 2027 inflation is closer to the 3.2% adverse scenario than the 2.5% baseline presented 10 September.
Berenberg and most other commentators expect a hold, followed by a hike most likely on 17 December.
Four-month low, down from 53.1 in September. It could signal slowing growth momentum.

macro_indicators.indicator: ECB consumer survey one-year inflation expectations
macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 3.0% in August and 2.9% in July, but well below the 4% of March and April. Berenberg sees expectations as fairly anchored relative to energy prices.
Reflects France's worsening fundamentals. Berenberg says it is not yet close to a full-blown crisis.
Smaller widening than France, consistent with contagion concerns that the TPI is designed to address.

risk_factors: Further oil price spikes could push Eurozone inflation above 4% and raise 2027 inflation toward the ECB's 3.2% adverse scenario.
A disorderly French yield spread blowout beyond what fundamentals warrant could force ECB action such as the TPI or verbal intervention.
Renewed US-Iran military escalation after the 3 November midterms could affect energy prices.
A sharper loss of Eurozone growth momentum, as hinted by the October composite PMI at 51.9.
Political risk from the French presidential election in April/May 2027, and uncertainty over the succession to Lagarde and three Executive Board vacancies.
vol_and_positioning: French 10-year yields are up 78bp and Italian 10-year yields up 38bp since 8 September, while the Bund yield is near its level of six weeks ago. This implies a wider French and Italian spread to Germany.
geopolitical: De-facto closure of the Strait of Hormuz has driven energy prices higher since the Iran war began about eight months ago.
The US may renew attacks on Iran after the 3 November midterm elections, followed by negotiations. Berenberg says the Hormuz situation may or may not change.
Berenberg describes France's creeping fiscal and political crisis. Marine Le Pen could win the French presidential election in April/May 2027, and the EU is trying to guard against that risk.
Leadership changes at the ECB are timed around the French election. Lagarde is likely to leave early, with her successor appointed while Macron is still president.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: headline inflation is at a three-year high of 3.8%, may briefly top 4%, and 2027 inflation could be near the ECB's 3.2% adverse scenario. Berenberg expects another 25bp hike on 17 December.
tension_points.bear_case: Berenberg sees little evidence of second-round effects, falling PMI output price inflation, and consumer inflation expectations well below the March and April 4%. A central bank cannot prevent the direct impact of external energy shocks, and higher French and Italian yields already restrain activity.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A decline in oil prices over next year, visible by the March 2027 ECB meeting, would likely end the hike-pause pattern, with the ECB staying on hold through 2027.

theme_stances.key_argument: The ECB has delivered both 2026 hikes alongside new staff projections, so it likely pauses on 29 October and hikes on 17 December.

theme_stances.key_argument: The ECB has no mandate and no appetite to fund French fiscal policy and would support France only if Paris returns to more sustainable policies.
theme_stances.evidence: the ECB has no mandate and no appetite to fund French fiscal follies
